assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect opened a whole field in which band topology, rather than symmetry breaking, classifies phases of matter. The central idea is simple and general: a bulk gap with protected edge or surface states. Theory and experiment fit together cleanly, and the concept has spread to photonics, cold atoms, mechanics and superconductors. This is the kind of unifying mechanism I value most.
assessment.attribution: The Kane-Mele proposal of the Z2 invariant and quantum spin Hall state is decisive on the theory side, and Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells. Hasan's three-dimensional topological insulator experiments are also important, but the three-person limit forces a choice. I would prefer Kane, Mele and Molenkamp. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (HgTe prediction) and Fu-Kane-Mele are not credited here, and this is a real credit problem I cannot resolve from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Over fifteen years of independent confirmation, including transport and ARPES in many materials. The interpretation is stable and the field is mature. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: The prediction of the HgTe quantum spin Hall state by Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang is not among the credited names, so the theory-experiment credit chain is incomplete.
Hasan and Molenkamp contributions are of different kinds (3D versus 2D), and a fair split is uncertain.
My recollection of priority details between the Kane-Mele and Bernevig-Zhang papers is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution turned the foundations of quantum mechanics into a cryptographic protocol whose security rests on physical law, and it launched quantum information science as an applied field. Originality is high, and the protocols are clear and simple. The impact runs from tabletop experiments to satellite links and networks. From a statistical physics view the information-theoretic framing of measurement is attractive.
assessment.attribution: BB84 by Bennett and Brassard and the entanglement-based protocol by Ekert are the conceptual cornerstones. Jian-Wei Pan has led the large experimental implementations (satellite QKD, networks), which are mostly engineering-scale demonstrations of existing protocols. I would credit the three theorists and note that the experimental side is a separate matter. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is not credited and priority is a recognised subtlety.
assessment.maturity: The protocols date to 1984 and 1991, and many experimental confirmations exist. Practical security (device imperfections, side channels) is still under work, but the physics is mature. The 2022 prize for entanglement experiments leaves some overlap in the field, though not in the specific discovery.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2022 physics prize on entanglement and Bell tests may count against it.
Whether deployed QKD is a physics discovery or an engineering application is open.
Wiesner's conjugate coding and the credit to Pan are unresolved allocation questions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The fluctuation theorems are exact relations that hold arbitrarily far from equilibrium. They extend the second law and linear-response theory to small, fluctuating systems, and they are simple and universal in the way I find most convincing. They are tested in single-molecule pulling experiments, colloids and quantum devices, and they underlie stochastic thermodynamics.
assessment.attribution: Several people stand behind the results. Evans, Cohen and Morriss (with Gallavotti and Cohen) found the steady-state fluctuation theorem. Jarzynski derived the work equality, and Crooks the detailed fluctuation theorem. Only Evans is credited here from the first group, and Searles, Cohen, Gallavotti and Kurchan are not on the list. That makes a clean three-person prize hard.
assessment.maturity: The theorems are well established and checked in many experiments, so the interpretation is stable. The field is mature and recognition would be timely, although the Nobel precedent for statistical-mechanics theory of this kind is thin.
uncertainties: Priority among Evans, Cohen, Morriss, Gallavotti, Jarzynski, Crooks and Kurchan is disputed and the supplied credit list is incomplete.
Whether the committee sees this as a discovery in physics or as a mathematical result remains open.
The experimental tests, mostly on biomolecules, may be seen as lying at the boundary of physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices became clean, tunable quantum simulators of Hubbard-type models, including the superfluid-Mott transition, and they allow direct observation of many-body quantum states with single-site resolution. The idea that one controllable quantum system can emulate another links condensed matter, statistical physics and quantum information. The impact is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Jaksch, Zoller and collaborators proposed the Bose-Hubbard realisation and Cirac and Zoller developed the broader theory of quantum simulation; Greiner and Bloch demonstrated the Mott transition and developed the quantum gas microscope. Hofstetter and others, and Hänsch and Esslinger, also contributed and are not credited here, as are the Jaksch and Greiner-Mandel collaborators. Choosing Zoller, Bloch and Greiner leaves out Cirac, who shares much of the theory credit.
assessment.maturity: The 2002 Mott insulator observation has been repeated and extended in many laboratories. Digital and analogue quantum simulation now go beyond this and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is mature, but the quantum-simulation payoff for new physics is still developing.
uncertainties: Theory credit between Zoller, Cirac and Jaksch is not cleanly separable.
Overlap with the 2001 Bose-Einstein condensation prize and with the neighbouring trapped-ion candidates.
Whether the most important outcome, quantum simulation of novel phases, has yet been delivered.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation as an organising principle in cells is a change of viewpoint, since cellular compartments without membranes behave like droplets of a condensed phase. It brings soft-matter and statistical physics concepts such as nucleation, surface tension and coarsening into cell biology. I find this attractive because a general physical mechanism explains diverse phenomena.
assessment.attribution: Brangwynne and Hyman showed liquid-like behaviour of P granules, with Jülicher providing the physical theory in that work and later on active droplets. Whether a physics prize would honour mainly biological observations is a question. Others such as Rosen, Brangwynne's collaborators, and Banani are not credited, and the allocation between biology and physics is unclear.
assessment.maturity: The field is young, about fifteen years, and expanding. Debates continue about which cellular structures are truly liquid, the physiological role of condensates, and the role of artefacts in in-vitro experiments. Recognition could be premature for physics.
uncertainties: Whether the field is judged to be physics or biology or chemistry by the Academy.
Some claims are contested, for instance the generality of phase separation in vivo.
Role of Jülicher relative to the experimental discoverers is a matter of judgment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene gave a tunable platform with flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity, and with it a new field (moire quantum matter). The prediction of flat bands at a specific twist angle followed by experimental discovery is a clean theory-experiment story.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the magic angle with a continuum model, and Jarillo-Herrero's group discovered correlated insulator and superconducting states in 2018. These are the decisive names. Earlier work, for example by Lopes dos Santos, Peres and Castro Neto, on twisted-graphene flat bands is not credited, and may need attention.
assessment.maturity: Seven to eight years old. Independent confirmation is extensive, but the nature of the superconductivity and the correlated states is still debated, so the interpretation is not yet stable. Probably premature for the time being.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism in the superconducting phase remains unsettled.
Priority claims regarding the early continuum models for twisted graphene.
Sample-dependence and reproducibility questions persist.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combines the magic-wavelength trapping idea with large ensembles of atoms. It has pushed fractional uncertainty to the 10^-18 level, with consequences for tests of fundamental physics, relativistic geodesy and a possible redefinition of the second. It is conceptually elegant and clearly quantitative.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the first clock, and Ye's group developed the highest-performance systems and many-body physics in them. Two laureates fit well. The 2005 and 2012 prizes honoured frequency combs and ion trapping, and Ye was a collaborator on combs, so allocation relative to Hall and Hänsch is not an issue for this candidate, but it is a context point.
assessment.maturity: Many independent clocks worldwide reach comparable accuracy, and the technology is mature. The redefinition of the second is pending, so full impact is still in the future.
uncertainties: Close overlap in the community with the 2005 frequency comb prize.
Whether the next jump in impact (redefinition of the second, new physics searches) has yet occurred.
Contributions of other groups, for example Lemonde, Le Targat and Takamoto, are not credited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics created a platform for strong light-matter coupling with superconducting qubits and microwave photons, and it is the basis for the leading solid-state quantum computing efforts. It is a clean realisation of cavity QED concepts in a scalable circuit.
assessment.attribution: Blais proposed the architecture with Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf, and Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in 2004. Girvin, Huang and the Yale group are partly absent from the list. Credit is shared and hard to cut at three.
assessment.maturity: Experiments are well confirmed and widely reproduced. The 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in superconducting circuits has just recognised the nearby foundation, so the timing for this adjacent topic is uncertain and the field is still evolving toward fault tolerance.
uncertainties: The 2025 prize on superconducting circuits may weigh against another award this soon.
Girvin and Huang are not credited, so the theory credit is incomplete.
Whether the main significance lies in physics discovery or in technology development.
